quizzes.backend_description: Shows an equation with 3/9 equals a fraction with denominator 3 and an unknown numerator represented by an empty box.
solution: Equivalent fractions have the same value — you can get one from another by multiplying or dividing the top and bottom by the same number. $\\[1em]$ We need $\frac{3}{9} = \frac{?}{3}$.
Compare the denominators: $9$ becomes $3$, which is $3$ times smaller ($9 \div 3 = 3$). $\\[1em]$ Divide the top by the same factor: $\frac{3 \div 3}{9 \div 3} = \frac{1}{3}$.
The missing numerator is $1$, giving $\frac{3}{9} = \frac{1}{3}$.

solution: Equivalent fractions have the same value — you can get one from another by multiplying or dividing the top and bottom by the same number. $\\[1em]$ We need $\frac{24}{28} = \frac{6}{?}$.
Compare the numerators: $24$ becomes $6$, which is $4$ times smaller ($24 \div 4 = 6$). $\\[1em]$ Divide the bottom by the same factor: $\frac{24 \div 4}{28 \div 4} = \frac{6}{7}$.
The missing denominator is $7$, giving $\frac{24}{28} = \frac{6}{7}$.
